description: Scoring commands report logical timeline IDs directly; compare against merged database pooling and public snapshots.
notes: Both HTTP runs use the isolated public_live cache alias with production timeout/retry options. The initial uncorrected harness failed warmup and is excluded.
The opt-in profiling mode was added after the initial HTTP baseline; the default HTTP workload and spectator modules are unchanged.
One-minute phases contain 20 commands each. Tail percentiles are sensitive to individual outliers; the 100-viewer command p95 worsened despite a lower median.
Four matches is an additional after-only scenario; no paired baseline is claimed for it.
Use direct stage timers for cost attribution; cProfile parent totals did not reconcile with elapsed time in this runtime.
Profiles run 20 sequential service commands without HTTP traffic or consuming jobs. They include cProfile overhead; compare with other profiles, not HTTP latency.
Local Python 3.14.7 differs from production Python 3.13. No TLS, proxy, WAN, media or provider traffic; these are not production capacity limits.
The full backend suite ran separately from measured load.

environment.limitations: Local synthetic traffic; host-run API/worker/generator share CPU. No TLS, proxy, WAN, media or provider traffic. Each data container: 2 CPUs/1 GiB; PostgreSQL default 100 connections. Later phases have longer timelines and warmer caches.

profile_before.limitations: Twenty sequential service calls; cProfile overhead is included. No HTTP, spectator load or worker consumption. Use direct stage timers for attribution; cProfile parent totals may be distorted by async publication callbacks. SQL and stage times overlap. Locked body excludes commit and post-commit callbacks; row-lock SQL includes roundtrip time, not just contention.
